title: Built-in `StyleBox` subtypes do not invoke virtual methods
body:
### Tested versions

4.4.1.stable - 4.5.1.stable

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

A type that derives from one of the concrete `StyleBox` subtypes (e.g. `StyleBoxTexture`) does not call the virtual `StyleBox` methods (e.g. `_Draw`).
This makes it impossible to create functional subtypes of `StyleBox` subtypes.

If this is intentional and caused by some limitation, concrete implementation types should be made `sealed`.


<strike>
Closely related is that all virtual methods are implemented as stubs instead of relaying work to their non-virtual built-in counterparts by default.
This makes it difficult to manually invoke methods that may or may not be implemented by a C# subtype, requiring something along the lines of:

```cs
if (myBox is StyleBoxTexture or StyleBoxFlat /* or ... */) {
    myBox.Draw(/* ... */);
} else {
    myBox._Draw(/* ... */);
}
```
</strike>

Edit: Calling the non-underscore-prefixed `Draw` always results in the correct behavior.

### Steps to reproduce

Launch the project and observe that the type deriving from `StyleBox` has its virtual `_Draw` method invoked, while the type deriving from `StyleBoxTexture` does not, drawing itself normally as via the non-virtual `Draw` method.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[StyleBoxVirtualInvocationIssue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23684910/StyleBoxVirtualInvocationIssue.zip)
